answer: A way I keep fit and healthy is by going to the gym a few times a week, which has become an important part of my lifestyle. There is a small gym about ten minutes from our flat, and I usually go on Saturday, Monday and Wednesday evenings after work, for roughly an hour each time. I started a couple of years ago, initially just to lose a little weight, but it soon became something I genuinely enjoy. At first I felt quite self-conscious, because everyone else seemed to know exactly what they were doing, but one of the trainers kindly showed me the basics. What works for me is having a set routine, which keeps me [[accountable]] and stops me making excuses. Beyond the obvious physical benefits, I find exercise incredibly [[therapeutic]] for my mental health. After a stressful day, a good workout is the perfect [[outlet]] for releasing tension. On the days I don't go, I still take a walk by the river, so I am rarely completely inactive, even during the busiest weeks. Honestly, the sense of discipline it has given me has spilled over into other areas of my life. I feel more energetic, sleep better and generally more positive. It required real commitment to make it a habit, but now I would feel restless without it. I think finding a form of exercise you actually enjoy is the key to [[sustaining]] it long term, and for me, the gym is exactly that, a routine I would find very hard to [[abandon]].

followUps.q: Do you ever go to the gym with a friend?
followUps.answer: Sometimes, with a university friend who lives nearby. Having a partner helps on days when I feel lazy, because I don't want to let him down, although we do end up chatting more than training.

followUps.q: Is going to the gym popular where you live?
followUps.answer: It is becoming more popular among young people, even in a modest town like Sirajganj. A few years ago there were hardly any gyms, but now several have opened, which shows how attitudes are changing.
